A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DART research, renamed DartControl in v2. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original motion-generation experiments, human preference results, spatial-control evaluations, and ablations in Tables 1–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations, revises control results, and adds a primitive-length ablation and qualitative physics-tracking and long-rollout findings.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds SMPL joint-reconstruction and joint-consistency terms to the stated VAE objective. Appendix G revises the controller reward specification, and Appendix H demonstrates optional PHC refinement. These are targeted changes within the retained latent-diffusion architecture and autoregressive control framework.

E1.justification: BABEL, HML3D, and the main generation/control tasks remain. V2 adds a physics-simulated crawling-refinement scenario in Appendix H and single-prompt long-rollout examples examining repeatable actions and action-completion boundaries in Appendix I.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets remain TEACH, DoubleTake, T2M-GPT*, FlowMDM, DNO, OmniControl, and GAMMA in their corresponding experiments. Appendix H/Figure 5 adds a qualitative comparison of raw DART output with PHC-refined output; PHC participates as a refinement method.

E3.justification: Appendix G changes the reported hopping weights from floor=100 and skate=10 to floor=10 and skate=100. Table 5 adds the H=2, F=16 configuration, and Appendix F reports comparisons of small initial noise variance, such as 0.01, against unit variance. These do not establish that every existing experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a longer-primitive ablation, a qualitative initialization-variance sensitivity observation, a PHC artifact-correction case study, and single-prompt rollout failure examples. The existing VAE, scheduled-training, per-frame, loss-weight, and diffusion-step analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use 95% confidence intervals in the quantitative tables and describe the same preference study with 256 sequences and three independent votes per comparison. No new seed counts, repeated-run protocol, or statistical testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 substantially revise control results. DART's in-between goal error changes from 0.54 to 0.59 cm; hopping skate changes from 41.18 to 2.22 cm/s, time from 13.89 to 20.50 s, and floor distance from 1.43 to 4.11 cm. Changed hopping weights and changed Table 3 dataset reference values prevent treating these as controlled performance gains. V2 also adds the F=16 ablation row and qualitative findings; Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces mathematical definitions for the added SMPL losses. Appendix G corrects the distance reward from current-minus-previous distance to previous-minus-current distance, making progress toward the goal positively rewarded. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: real-time text-conditioned autoregressive motion generation and spatial control through latent-noise optimization or reinforcement learning. Renaming and additional supporting material do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendices H–J substantially expand applicability limits beyond the retained coarse-label alignment problem: kinematic physical artifacts, fluctuations after finite actions reach their terminal states, and difficulty generalizing to open-vocabulary prompts. Appendix F also explains the smoothness-versus-diversity tradeoff from low-variance initialization. These materially qualify the scope of the generation capabilities.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies male bodies with zero shape parameters, the history frames used for goal and floor observations, the SMPL loss weight of 100 and its exclusion from denoiser training, and Gaussian initialization details. It explicitly identifies the existing project page as providing code and videos. Hardware information is retained and relocated.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive comparison with CLoSD concerning paired control-signal training data, alongside references including HumanMAC and AMD. The new appendices introduce PHC and literature on obtaining motion data and annotations from videos and generative models. Many other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 renames the paper DartControl, edits introduction and method passages, expands the diffusion explanation, standardizes human-preference terminology, and adds acknowledgements and appendix discussions. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive clearer component labels and annotations, Figure 5 adds the PHC comparison, and Table 5 gains an ablation row. The preference-study figure and algorithms shift placement, and the title/header adopts ICLR formatting. Existing scene-interaction and preference-interface images are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and interpretation through the corrected reward sign, fuller loss and implementation specifications, an additional horizon ablation, and substantive limitations. The gains are limited: revised control scores do not isolate improvements across versions, and hopping trades reduced skating for longer completion time and greater floor distance. The retained core evidence remains largely unchanged.
